entities.name: Query HIV-1 Env
observations: 768-residue viral envelope glycoprotein precursor sequence; contains ambiguous X residues, so some sequence-derived physicochemical calculations are unavailable.
Pfam GP120 domain spans residues 33–512 (i-Evalue 9.8e-193) and GP41 domain spans residues 531–721 (i-Evalue 1.2e-45).
Closest reviewed Swiss-Prot homologs are HIV-1 gp160 proteins P05881, P04579, and Q9Q714, with 74.4–77.1% identity and approximately 99.6–100% query coverage.
Architecture is consistent with an N-terminal signal peptide, large glycosylated gp120 ectodomain, gp41 fusion/transmembrane module, and cytoplasmic tail.

Homology-based function: precursor is cleaved by furin-like protease into gp120 and gp41; mature Env forms a trimeric gp120-gp41 spike, binds CD4 and chemokine coreceptors, and mediates viral membrane fusion.
Localization inferred from homologs: viral envelope and host-cell/endosomal membranes; single-pass type I membrane protein.
Evidence grade reported by protein analysis: moderate homology support; exact strain-specific receptor usage and cleavage positions are not established solely from this sequence.
Input contains multiple X residues, including near the ectodomain and cleavage-region vicinity; these may affect exact residue numbering and fine-grained motif interpretation.

entities.name: HIV-1 gp160
observations: Reviewed reference proteins P05881, P04579, and Q9Q714 annotate gp160 as a precursor cleaved into gp120 surface and gp41 transmembrane proteins.
Mature Env is a homotrimer of noncovalently associated gp120-gp41 heterodimers and functions as a class I viral fusion protein.
Reference annotations describe CD4 attachment followed by chemokine-coreceptor engagement, commonly CCR5 or CXCR4, and fusion with host plasma or endosomal membranes.
Reference topology includes an N-terminal signal peptide, extracellular/luminal glycoprotein region, one transmembrane helix, and cytoplasmic tail.
